# Ornstein Uhlenbeck Spread Backtest 

In order to show that the OU process can be applied to pairs trading we will first construct a synthetic spread and then move to real life data. For real pairs, we first investigate a linear spread, given two asset price series. We then fit the OU model to the observed spread.

## Backtest on Synthetic Spread

Let us generate an OU process and treat it as if it were an observed spread.

Take $\theta = 2, \mu = 0, \sigma = 1$.

```{python}
import ornstein_uhlenbeck.ou as ou
from ornstein_uhlenbeck.estimation import estimate_parameters
import ornstein_uhlenbeck.utils as utils
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import plotly.io

params = ou.OUParams(
    theta = 2.0,
    mu = 0.0,
    sigma = 1.0
)

x0 = 0.0
dt = 0.01
n_steps = 20000
n_paths = 1

rng = np.random.default_rng(50)

t = ou.time_grid(dt, n_steps)
path = ou.simulate_paths(x0, params, dt, n_steps, n_paths, rng)

fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(
    go.Scatter(
        x = t,
        y = path[:,0],
        name = "Simulated path",
        mode = "lines",
    )
)

fig.add_hline(
    y = params.mu,
    line_dash = "dash",
    annotation_text = "Long-run mean",
)

fig.update_layout(
    title = "Single Ornstein-Uhlenbeck sample path",
    xaxis_title = "Time",
    yaxis_title = "State"
)

utils.apply_theme(fig)
fig.show()
```

We will now devise a trading rule. For the synthetic spread, we will define a standard threshold strategy based on deviations from the long-run mean.

In the stationary regime, the OU process has distribution

$$
S_t\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu,\frac{\sigma^2}{2\theta}).
$$

Thus in stationarity, the stationary standard deviation is

$$
\sigma_S=\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{2\theta}}.
$$

Define thresholds in terms of stationary standard deviations as follows:

- Long spread if $S_t\lt\mu-2\sigma_S$
- Short spread if $S_t\gt\mu+2\sigma_S$
- Exit when $S_t$ returns to $\mu$

We use the first 75% of the synthetic OU process as training data to estimate the parameters and will subsequently trade the strategy on the remaining 25% to avoid look-ahead bias.

```{python}
split_index = int(0.75 * len(path))

train = path[:split_index]
test = path[split_index - 1:]

t_train = t[:split_index]
t_test = t[split_index - 1:]

# REMOVE LATER ONCE INITIAL_PARAMS IS BUILT INTO ESTIMATE_PARAMETERS

m = train.mean()

initial_params = [5, m, 5]

result = estimate_parameters(train[:, 0], t_train)

estimated_params = ou.OUParams(
    theta=result.x[0],
    mu=result.x[1],
    sigma=result.x[2],
)

print(estimated_params)

stationary_std = ou.stationary_std(estimated_params)
upper_threshold = estimated_params.mu + 2 * stationary_std
lower_threshold = estimated_params.mu - 2 * stationary_std

positions = np.zeros(len(test))
position = 0

for i, spread in enumerate(test[:, 0]):
    if position == 0:
        if spread < lower_threshold:
            position = 1
        elif spread > upper_threshold:
            position = -1

    elif position == 1:
        if spread >= estimated_params.mu:
            position = 0

    elif position == -1:
        if spread <= estimated_params.mu:
            position = 0

    positions[i] = position

spread = test[:, 0]

pnl = positions[:-1] * np.diff(spread)
cumulative_pnl = np.cumsum(pnl)
final_pnl = cumulative_pnl[-1]

print(final_pnl)
```

For this strategy we will define the number of trades as one complete entry-to-exit cycle.

```{python}
trade_pnls = []
in_trade = False
trade_pnl = 0.0

for i, position in enumerate(positions[:-1]):

    if not in_trade and position != 0:
        # Enter trade
        in_trade = True
        trade_pnl = pnl[i]

    elif in_trade and position != 0:
        # Continue holding
        trade_pnl += pnl[i]

    elif in_trade and position == 0:
        # Exit trade
        trade_pnls.append(trade_pnl)
        in_trade = False
        trade_pnl = 0.0

number_of_trades = len(trade_pnls)
average_trade_pnl = np.mean(trade_pnls)

winning_trades = sum(trade_pnl > 0 for trade_pnl in trade_pnls)

if number_of_trades > 0:
    win_rate = winning_trades / number_of_trades
else:
    win_rate = 0.0


print(f"Number of trades: {number_of_trades}")
print(f"Average PnL per trade: {average_trade_pnl}")
print(f"Win rate: {win_rate:.2%}")
```

Note that for the win rate here, only completed trades are included.

```{python}
fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(
    go.Scatter(
        x = t_test[1:],
        y = cumulative_pnl,
        name = "Synthetic PnL accumulation",
        mode = "lines",
    )
)

fig.update_layout(
    title = "Synthetic PnL Accumulation",
    xaxis_title = "Time",
    yaxis_title = "Cumulative PnL"
)

utils.apply_theme(fig)
fig.show()

running_max = np.maximum.accumulate(cumulative_pnl)
drawdown = cumulative_pnl - running_max
max_drawdown = drawdown.min()

print(f"Maximum Drawdown: {max_drawdown}")

fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(
    go.Scatter(
        x = t_test[1:],
        y = drawdown,
        name = "Synthetic Drawdown Accumulation",
        mode = "lines",
    )
)

fig.update_layout(
    title = "Synthetic Strategy Drawdown",
    xaxis_title = "Time",
    yaxis_title = "Drawdown"
)

utils.apply_theme(fig)
fig.show()
```
